title: Stored Procedures & Data Pipelines
interviewAnswer: Stored procedures package database-side logic such as selection, joins and transformations. In data pipelines, orchestration tools can call these procedures and move their outputs to downstream stages.
why: Stored procedures appear in enterprise data systems and are relevant when explaining SQL-centric ETL experience.
intuition: A stored procedure packages database-side SQL logic behind a callable name so applications or orchestrators can execute a consistent transformation close to the data.
deepDive: Procedures can contain parameterized queries, branching, temporary tables, transactions and error handling. Benefits include centralized logic and reduced data movement; drawbacks include vendor coupling, harder versioning/testing and hidden business logic if poorly managed. Orchestrators such as ADF can call procedures as pipeline activities.
workedExample: A new user story requires data from several tables. A procedure joins/filters them into the required shape; ADF triggers the procedure and moves the output to the next pipeline stage.
code:
-- conceptual
CREATE PROCEDURE get_customer_features @as_of DATE AS
SELECT ...
FROM a JOIN b ON ...
WHERE event_date <= @as_of;
commonMistakes: Putting every business rule into opaque database procedures with no version control.
Building dynamic SQL unsafely from user input.
Confusing a stored procedure with the orchestration pipeline itself.
followUps: Why execute logic in the database?
How would ADF call a procedure?
How do you debug a failing pipeline activity?
production: Keep SQL/procedure definitions in source control, test with representative data, log parameters/run IDs and separate database logic from orchestration concerns.
